approved: Primary Industries Levies and Charges Disbursement Bill 2023
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would set new rules for how organisations that receive levies and charges from primary industries can spend the money.
Spending would be restricted to specific categories: marketing, research and development, general purposes, Commonwealth costs, refunds, debts, and activities prescribed in the rules.
The rules could require that marketing or R&D money collected for a particular industry sector be spent only for that sector's benefit.
Consolidates spending requirements from separate legislation into one consistent set for all declared recipient bodies.
Creates separate spending requirements for statutory recipient bodies.
Allows the rules to prescribe industry-specific activities on which marketing, R&D, or general amounts may be spent.
Permits the rules to require that marketing or R&D amounts be earmarked for the benefit of a particular primary industry sector.
Declared recipient bodies that receive levy and charge amounts from primary industries.
